title: FOX AI cochlear-implant fitting matches or beats manual fitting in a 24-patient crossover RCT in Brussels
summary: In a Brussels crossover RCT, newly implanted patients fitted with FOX had better speech intelligibility at 3 and 12 months; all manual-arm patients kept the FOX map; 47 experienced users improved.
account: Wathour et al. (Ear and Hearing, published online 21 December 2022) ran a one-year randomised crossover trial of 24 newly implanted cochlear-implant patients at Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc, Brussels, comparing manual fitting with the Fitting to Outcome eXpert (FOX): from 3 months the FOX group showed less variability and better speech intelligibility in quiet and noise, with median phoneme scores of 50%, 70% and 50% at 55, 70 and 85 dB SPL versus 45%, 50% and 40%; after crossover, 100% of the manual group kept the FOX map and 82% performed better with it, while 63% of the FOX group preferred their manual map for comfort. A companion study (Otology & Neurotology, 18 January 2023) gave 47 experienced users a FOX map and found median improvements of 10 dB at 6,000 Hz and 10% in phonemic discrimination and speech scores after 15 days of take-home use. Two 2019 case studies from the same group reported improved word recognition with AI suggestions in one of two adults. Otoconsult's site describes FOX as an outcome-based application assisting audiologists and AI-FOX as the successor of a deterministic first-generation tool. P. J. Govaerts co-authored all three papers; whether any author is affiliated with Otoconsult could not be verified from the fetched records. The date is the Ear and Hearing publication date.
purpose: Recommend cochlear-implant MAP settings to audiologists from measured auditory outcomes
system: FOX (Fitting to Outcome eXpert) / AI-FOX cochlear-implant fitting software
model_version: Generation used in the 2022-2023 studies not stated; Otoconsult describes AI-FOX as successor to a deterministic first-generation FOX
taxonomy_note: Cohort and small-RCT evidence rather than an individual case; the earlier verifier wanted an individual peer-reviewed case and could not verify the authors' independence from the developer. The JMIR 2026 medical-captioning pilot (simulated encounters) and deep-neural-network hearing-aid laboratory cohorts named in the same reason are not recorded here. Author independence from Otoconsult remains unverified; the papers are marked independent on the fetched affiliations only.

ratings.reason: Better speech intelligibility at 3 and 12 months in newly implanted patients; median 10% gains in speech scores for experienced users.
Authors report the FOX approach equivalent or superior in 'hearing performance, comfort, and resources'.

ai_role.statement: The software proposes MAP settings from measured outcomes; the trials compare it with manual fitting and attribute the measured gains to the FOX maps. All three papers share co-author P. J. Govaerts and the developer's identity is taken from Otoconsult's own site; no record independent of the authors' group was fetched.
